sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic only: names, location, extinction 1920s, sources Delafosse 1904, Tauxier 1924, Paperno 2008, mandelang site.

sources.citation: Kunstkamera Mande-languages site (Vydrin et al.), page 'Gbin' (French), archived 2011 and 2017; live URL now 404.
sources.note: Nothing; states Gbin documentation is 'quelques douzaines de mots et de phrases' in Delafosse 1904 and the numerals in Tauxier; links Paperno 2008 PDF.

sources.citation: Paperno, Denis. 2011. One Hundred Years Old Language Documentation: Preliminary Notes on the Gbin Language. WALC handout, 3 pp. (English version of the above)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; states the Gbin corpus is 'mostly a wordlist and few sentences; the number of words in his data is just about 100'; discusses only historical consonantism and subgrouping.
sources.venue: WALC handout, 3 pp. (English version of the above)

sources.citation: Paperno, Denis. n.d. [c. 2011]. Jazyk gbin: predvaritel'nye nabljudenija [The Gbin language: preliminary observations]. In: Le monde Mandé: collected papers in honour of Valentin Vydrin. St Petersburg. 6 pp. (Glottolog ref 318729)
sources.note: Sections: data sources, fate of Gbin and South Mande, Gbin in cross-linguistic comparison (historical consonant correspondences *k>w, *d>z, *t>z, *c>d, *w>ŋ), conclusion. No mention of stress, accent or tone (a full-text search for stress/accent ударен/акцент/тон finds nothing relevant).

sources.citation: Paperno, Denis. 2008. Modern Beng and the linguistic materials of Tauxier and Delafosse [= Parlers décrits par Tauxier et Delafosse et le Beng moderne de Ouassadougou]. In V. Vydrin (ed.), Langues et linguistique mandé: 2e Colloque international, St Petersbourg, 15-17 sept. 2008, pp. 113-120. (plus 6-pp. variant)
sources.note: About Beng dialects; Gbin appears only as a numeral column (Delafosse). Nothing on Gbin stress.
sources.venue: Langues et linguistique mandé: 2e Colloque international, St Petersbourg

sources.citation: Tauxier, Louis. 1921. Le noir de Bondoukou: Koulangos, Dyoulas, Abrons, etc. Paris: Ernest Leroux. (Livre VI, ch. 1 'Gbins, Gouros et Gans de l'Anno', pp. 363-364: Gbin-Gouro numerals 1-10 from one elderly semi-speaker, side by side with Delafosse's 1902 forms)
sources.note: Nothing; only ten numerals in French orthography and ethnographic/census notes.

sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1904. Vocabulaires comparatifs de plus de 60 langues ou dialectes parlés à la Côte d'Ivoire et dans les régions limitrophes, avec des notes linguistiques et ethnologiques. Paris: Ernest Leroux. (Gbin: ethnographic note p. 146; collection note p. 148; comparative wordlist and grammatical notes for Soninké/Bozo/Sya/Mouin/Gbin pp. 149-161)
sources.note: The only primary source on Gbin (c. 100 words, a few sentences, no tone or stress marks). Nothing on Gbin stress. General remark p. 3 (all languages of the volume): 'Quant à l'accent tonique ou plutôt l'intonation.. il est impossible de donner ces indications au moyen de signes alphabétiques. Des notes spéciales indiqueront les cas principaux'; no such note is given for Gbin. p. 159: interrogation marked only by 'intonation' (phrase-level, all five languages).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page gbin1239 (references: only Delafosse 1904; no phonology/grammar refs)
sources.note: Nothing; AES status extinct; the three other Glottolog-listed refs (Kisilier 2017 on Tsakonian, Jakobson 1958 on Slavic) are title-string false hits on 'predvaritel'nye nabljudenija'.
